deviations:
1. Resume: commit 8b6f1d4d (KBA-06) came from the interrupted attempt. I reviewed the diff against the card and re-ran its tests against both main's source (red) and the worktree (green); I kept it unchanged.
2. I amended my own just-created KBA-08 commit once (message only: Co-Authored-By trailer changed to the model-named form the harness reminder asks for; 39852fd2 became 2a1deb3b). No commit of the earlier attempt was touched. All three commits carry `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` plus the Claude-Session trailer, not the bare `Claude` form of the brief; the brief says the orchestrator normalises this.
3. KBA-08 follows the inventory design and widens the generic token to `version (1[5-9][0-9]{2}|2004)`. Consequence beyond the card's list: every name with the token 'Version 2004' now derives release 2004, including 'Windows Server, version 2004 (Server Core installation)' (still no key, as the 1903/1909 server names), so that name's scope id changes too. It is stated in the spec amendment, the audit line and a test. A differential run of 2,352 generated names between main and the fix showed changes only for names with that token or of the exact release-less client form.
4. The implied-release pattern also accepts 'Windows 10 for ARM64-based Systems' and 'Windows 11 for 32-bit Systems' (products that never shipped); the resolver's architecture gate still blocks non-amd64 pairing.
5. D-DEF-04: leads.py receives the engine's reason only as text and cli_leads.py (the adapter) is not an owned file, so the two cases are told apart by the reason's prefix 'Stored ranking' (constant STORED_RANKING_REASON). The test reads the real reasons through RealEngine so a reworded pipeline reason fails there.
6. The synergy golden was not changed: rows with an attached context keep their text.

open_risks: KBA-08 bumps ALIAS_CATALOG_VERSION to 2. Because product-start admission and journal repair compare the full stored ProductScope (alias_catalog_version included), every product-start selection that is still pending in a workspace journal from catalog 1 is refused with PT-KBC-STALE and must be repeated, not only selections on the re-keyed names. This is the existing guard (tests/test_kb_product_start_20261106.py::test_product_context_repair_refuses_changed_alias_interpretation) but it reaches wider than the changed names.

Stored investigations whose scope is one of the changed names (release-less Windows 10/11 client form, or any name with 'Version 2004', the server name included) get the 'repeat the search' refusal from `kb products` / `kb pairs`. Covered by a test for the Windows 10 name only; the 2004 and server names take the same code path but have no end-to-end test.

The release-less Windows 11 name now merges into the existing 11-21H2 scope of the same architecture. That is intended, but it rests on the assumption that MSRC's 'Windows 11 for x64-based Systems' means 21H2, which I could not check offline.

A contrived name carrying both a server year and 'Version 2004' (e.g. 'Windows Server 2019 Version 2004') now derives release 2004 instead of 2019, the same precedence 'Version 1909' already had. I know of no vendor name of that shape.

D-DEF-04 classification depends on the pipeline reasons starting with 'Stored ranking'. The 'Stored ranking is incomplete' reason is classified by reading the source only; my test produces the no-run, empty, project-changed and older-algorithm reasons, not the incomplete one.

In the no-advisory state the code-change chip still reads 'detector signals (...) do not align with any applicable CVE' and the applicability chip keeps state 'neutral'. I changed only the two texts the card names.
